qt: to the Commission Elena Kountoura (The Left) Subject:

Every year, more than 35 000 people in the EU die from infections caused by microorganisms resistant to antimicrobial drugs. In addition, 4.3 million patients each year contract at least one hospital-acquired infection during their hospital stay. The European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) warns that the EU is off track to meet the targets of the Council Recommendation on combating antimicrobial resistance under the One Health approach by 20301, as infections from some resistant bacteria continue to increase2. Of particular concern is the situation in Greece, where the highest antibiotic consumption is consistently recorded among the Member States, with a significant deviation from the European average3. Having regard to the ECDC report on Greece, according to which the previous National Action Plan 2019-2023 was not implemented4: 1.
What European measures does the Commission intend to take to reverse the increasing trend of infections caused by resistant bacteria and achieve the 2030 targets?

Does the Commission intend to strengthen pan-European information and awarenessraising actions on antimicrobial resistance and the rational use of antibiotic medicines, and to support the continuous training and education of healthcare professionals?

Has the Commission been informed about the National Action Plan of Greece on antimicrobial resistance 2026-2030, the implementation measures, the timetable, the available resources and the measurable targets, and how its implementation is monitored?

Of the five targets, only the one for reducing MRSA infections has been achieved, while the others for reducing antibiotic consumption, consumption of at least 65 % of Access-category antibiotics and reducing resistant E.coli and resistant K.pneumoniae infections are not on track to be achieved. 2 Resistant E.coli infections increased by 16.4 % and resistant K.pneumoniae by 72 %, significantly deviating from the respective reduction targets of 10 % and 5 % by 2030. 3 Greece records the highest antibiotic consumption in the EU from 2022 to date. In 2025, 31.1 daily prescribed doses per 1000 inhabitants were recorded, compared to the European average of 18.9 (https://www.ecdc.europa.eu/en/publications-data/antimicrobial-consumption-eueea-esac-net-annualepidemiological-report-2025). 4 The report states that insufficient funding had been secured and a clear timetable was lacking, while since then there has been little or no information on the new National Action Plan 2026-2030. 1
